fields.AN_Notes: Thematic analysis of 63 FAccT and AIES papers, evaluated in a workshop with AI experts. Bias axes follow the work's own worked example in the introduction (Black women and image recognition, racially profiled Black woman); the welfare cases (dual nationality, low-income and immigrant backgrounds) are cited cases and stay uncoded as axes. Harm types: the harms named (welfare fraud scandals, Gender Shades error disparities, COMPAS) are cited cases that the work's own argument does not establish, and the five themes structure recommendations, not harm types, so None. Mitigation: all five themes are organisational (interdisciplinary teams, positionality statements, community co-ownership, power analysis, documentation of data and metrics). The workshop gauged perceived actionability of intermediate recommendation versions, not the effect of an applied mitigation, so the status stays Proposed. Gender is treated only within the intersectional frame and is not defined; race, not gender, is explicitly called a social construct, so Social_Construct is not coded. AN_Task None because the work addresses AI development practice, not AI use for a professional task.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

fields.AN_Notes: Systematic review of 67 social work AI articles with a proposed Unified Model of Artificial Intelligence Enhanced Social Work along Staub-Bernasconi's triple mandate. Child welfare is the dominant practice area of the reviewed literature (RQ1a), while the model addresses social work in general, so AN_Population is General_Social_Work. Bias axes: indigenous peoples, younger people and the poor appear only as an enumeration of cited under- or over-represented groups, so None. Harm types: the synthesis theme Data and Algorithmic Injustice names exclusion, invisibility, stigmatisation and discrimination as cited consequences without structuring them as harm types, so None. AN_Task: decision support and predictive risk assessment (profession level), text mining for social work research, and agency resource allocation and data exchange (Administration). Mitigation proposals: inclusive data sets (Pre_Processing) and governance, oversight, participation, training and interdisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Bias is not defined; its understanding follows the human-rights principle of nondiscrimination. AI Agent Review: AN_Harm_Types None. The synthesis theme 'Data and Algorithmic Injustice' is a section of the review, but it is organised as injustice in general and lists consequences (exclusion, injustice, prejudices, stigmatization and discrimination, invisibility) each taken from a cited study; no harm type structures the synthesis as a section, table row or coded category, and the groups concerned stand in an enumeration that also leaves AN_Bias_Axes at None.

fields.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (poverty/wealth, criminal/law enforcement, immigrant/citizen, worker/executive, ideologies, everyday scenarios), followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is a research instrument; the recommendation that users be more conscious of the prompts they use is Recommended_Practice without a codable technique, so AN_Prompt_Techniques is None. Language_Culture covers cultural context and Global North hegemony in depictions of food and settings; Physical_Appearance covers body size and conventional attractiveness. Mitigation proposals: better curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), and algorithmic reparation, regulation, criminal culpability and diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all proposed. Studientyp Empirisch rather than Experimentell because the prompt contrasts serve an interpretative analysis without a controlled comparison. The confederate flag is discussed as violent imagery, but Toxicity is not coded because the codebook ties it to language. AN_Task None because the work audits a general image generator without a professional application task. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only: the passages after Guillaumin and on intersectionality determine power systems and the interplay of oppressions, not bias or discrimination, and the work sets 'biases' in quotation marks without determining it. Fairness teilweise rests on the recommendations structured around algorithmic reparation as a foundation for building, evaluating and adjusting machine learning systems, with deliberate intervention and training data curation, a subordinate treatment of fair system design.
